root_idea.summary: The root centers on the olive and its expressed oil, with related lexical uses for applying, preparing, supplying, and seeking oil.
root_idea.development: The concrete noun زيت denotes olive oil, while the related terms زيتون and زيتونة denote the olive tree or its fruit and the individual tree; derived verbs extend the root to anointing, seasoning, provisioning, self-anointing, and requesting oil.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Quran-attested noun denoting olive oil.
Distinct Quran-attested singulative noun for an individual olive tree.
Distinct Quran-attested collective noun for the olive tree or its fruit.

senses.definition: Olive oil, the expressed juice of the olive.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, the noun appears possessively in reference to the oil belonging to the olive tree.
The singulative counterpart of the collective زيتون; the Quranic occurrence is in the lamp parable of 24:35.

senses.definition: The olive, as a collective term for the olive tree and its fruit.
senses.usage_conditions: The collective noun has the singulative زيتونة. In Quranic usage, the referent may be the tree or its fruit according to context; the supplied English gloss does not by itself resolve that distinction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To anoint someone or something with olive oil.
To put olive oil into food, or to prepare, moisten, or mix food with it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported of food, bread, or crumbled bread.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feed people with oil, or to use oil as the seasoning of their food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A food-provisioning use of the Form I verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To furnish someone with oil as travelling provision.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II verb; the oil is supplied as provisions for a journey.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have much oil, or for one's oil to become abundant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV verb describing abundance or increase of oil.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To anoint oneself with olive oil.
To seek or demand oil, including by requesting it as a gift.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form X verb of seeking or requesting oil.

other_classical_meanings.definition: By extension, any oil; also the choicest or essential part of a thing, figuratively its “marrow.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The general-oil application is noted as current usage, while the choicest-constituent value is a rare lexical extension.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A technical name for Lapis Judaicus, a stone resembling an olive and found in Judaea.
Of or relating to the olive; olive-coloured.
A seller or presser of oil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Agent noun; the oil may be olive oil or, in colloquial usage, any oil.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A conventional expression for someone arriving in dirty clothes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the idiom جَاءَ فُلَانٌ فِي ثِيَابِ زَيَّاتٍ, literally referring to the clothes of an oil seller or presser.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Food into which oil has been put or with which it has been prepared.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes food made or treated with oil.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who anoints themself with oil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Nominal descriptor for a person characterized by self-anointing with oil; the wording does not impose a gender restriction.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Putting oil into or mixing it with food.
Feeding or seasoning food with oil.
Olive oil is covered by the Quranic sense; general oil and choicest-constituent extensions are covered classically.
Olive tree and fruit, with the singulative زيتونة, are represented under the Quranic forms.
One who anoints themself with oil.
Diminutive statement only; it adds no independent lexical meaning.

cautions: زَيْتُون is a collective noun whose referent may be the olive tree or its fruit; زيتونة is its individually specified form. The Quranic contextual glosses do not always resolve that distinction.
